claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, Administration placed before City Council or a Council committee, on a published agenda, at least two distinct proposals to change snow and ice control service, each stating new spending to deliver it.
claims.interpretation_notes: I count the Fall 2025 Improved Accessibility service package and the Well Maintained City package as two distinct proposals. The Fall 2025 package develops the Option 3 response to CO03079; I treat that later package as one proposal, not a second proposal in addition to its originating options report. CO03513 was listed on an agenda captured on 2026-08-22, before the comment date, although the committee first dealt with it on 2026-08-31. MATERIAL FRAMING CONCERN: The primary rule treats an item published on a future meeting agenda as already put to a body. That makes the count two and the verdict Supported; requiring a body to have dealt with the item by 2026-08-27 leaves one and changes the verdict to Partially supported. The reader-facing phrase “already asked council” should carry that timing qualification. Under the primary rule, the identified count is P=2, C=2, U=0. Identified proposals: Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair, DocumentId 278877, City Council item 7.2, first listed on the 2025-11-24 agenda; $9.938 million in 2026 operating costs in the budget attachment, with the package description also stating a $2.11 million one-time capital investment. The source says no funding existed in the 2025 and 2026 budgets for enhancements, but does not state an approved snow-control budget figure and the increase against it. Well Maintained City, DocumentId 304812, Community and Public Services Committee item 7.1, agenda captured 2026-08-22; approximately $23.6 million annually in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding. Its text does not identify an approved budget figure and increase against it. CO03513 Attachment 10 lists 24 separately costed optional enhancements; these are options within the report rather than separately presented service packages under the primary unit. Required alternatives: considered by a body by 2026-08-27: P=1, C=1, U=0, Partially supported; to 2026-10-02 under the primary timing rule: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; to 2026-10-02 with the considered-by-body rule: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; pre-election start 2025-01-01: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported, counting the CO03079 originating options and the later Fall package as one proposal; Council alone by 2026-08-27: P=1, C=1, U=0, Partially supported; separately costed options: at least 25 identified costed proposals/options (24 CO03513 enhancements plus the Fall package), all with stated new spending; exactly two count rule: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported. Under the stricter approved-budget-excess reading, the Fall package text says no enhancement funding existed in the 2025 and 2026 budgets, but the sources do not clearly state the approved snow-program budget figure and increment against it; CO03513 also lacks such a baseline. I therefore do not treat either proposal as established to exceed an identified approved budget on the required strict test.

limitations: Automated retrieval of the eScribe meeting and filestream pages was blocked or returned 403. I used the full carried text for reports, attachments, agendas and minutes where supplied, and attempted the named public URLs. No independent comparison of the August 22 archived agenda's DocumentIds and contents against the later live attachments was possible.

The CO03513 report and Attachments 9 and 10 are available here as carried text; the remaining attachments were not needed to establish the two identified costed packages. The report says the live agenda attachment identifiers were reposted, but source-content identity could not be independently checked.

The search surfaced Council agenda records for the January-February 2026 snow-service motions, March 17 motions, the November 2025 budget agenda, and the August 31 committee agenda. The full calendar of every Council and committee agenda in the period was not independently audited here, so the stated primary P count is the count of identified qualifying packages, not a guaranteed complete exact count.

The stricter approved-budget-excess alternative is less certain than the primary cost test. CO03079 says no 2025 and 2026 funding existed for enhancements, while the Fall package is labeled unfunded; the sources do not clearly state the approved snow-program budget figure and the package increase against that figure as the brief's strict rule requires.
unknowns: Whether other Council or committee agendas in the reference period listed additional Administration snow and ice service packages not surfaced in the carried meeting pages or web search.
Whether the agenda attachments reposted under new DocumentIds after 2026-08-22 have identical content.
Whether the City had an approved snow and ice control budget baseline stated elsewhere that could establish the strict alternative's required figure and increase.

calculations_needed: Primary identified packages: P=2, C=2, U=0; rung Supported.

New spending amounts are reported as published: CO03513 Well Maintained City, approximately $23.6 million annually ongoing operating plus $11.5 million one-time capital; FCS03158 Improved Accessibility, $9.938 million operating in 2026 and a package description stating $2.11 million one-time capital. These amounts cover different periods and components and should not be added into a single total.

CO03513 Attachment 10 lists 24 separately costed optional enhancements. Their individual amounts should be reported from that attachment rather than aggregated unless the article clearly labels the sum as a reviewer calculation.
Alternative considered by body by 2026-08-27: P=1, C=1, U=0; Partially supported. Other timing and window alternatives are stated in interpretation_notes.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A complete agenda search identifying a second qualifying package first listed after 2025-11-18 but not represented in the carried documents could alter the exact count and some alternatives.

Evidence that the Well Maintained City package was not in fact carried as an Administration proposal on the August 31 published agenda, or that the attachment's stated amounts were not new spending, could reduce the primary count below two.
A material correction to either package's text showing no incremental spending would change the primary verdict.
claims.suggested_one_line: By August 27, 2026, two costed snow-service packages had been placed on published Council or committee agendas, though only one had been considered by a body by that date.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Two identified packages stated new spending: the Fall 2025 active-pathway and sidewalk package, and the Well Maintained City package listed on the August 31, 2026 committee agenda. The second was on the agenda before August 27 but was not considered until August 31.
suggested_tldr: Primary reading: two identified costed packages were on published agendas by August 27, 2026.
Timing matters: only one had been considered by a body by the comment date.
The documents establish stated spending, but do not clearly establish each package's increase over an identified approved snow budget.
